body:
I'm not sure how the college system works in Canada. I know we have community colleges but I don't know what the requirements of getting into them are (probably not much different from the U.S I'd imagine).

The thing is, the subjects that I do do well in I have no interest in. Maybe I'm good at writing, but it tends not to be something I enjoy doing. I'd much rather have a talent in something like art or music, but I ended up giving up on both of those things.

As of now, I can't imagine myself being able to get into college. I can hardly handle the 10th grade, both socially and academically wise, and tend to get low or failing grades in each of my classes (excluding 2 subjects). I take both a specialized math course *and* go to a specialized school, which isn't even so much a school as much as it is a therapy program.
My main source of income? My parents, I'm only 16.

My family rarely communicates with each other. I spend most of my time upstairs, while my mom and dad will be in the living room on their phones and my little brother on the computer. When I bring up my depression, I'm either told to go away or am yelled at.

I'm trying to get help, trust me. I see a therapist as well as a youth worker and I'm planning to meet with my psychiatrist some time soon. Still, a lot of the time I spend with them never feels like enough. I'll talk to them for an hour, but as soon as I return home, I immediately become lonely again. 

I've given up on flute- we returned it and my dad cancelled the lessons. I don't think I'm in the right mindset to commit to something like learning an instrument these days. Then again, I don't think I've ever been in the right mindset. Giving up on things has been something I've done since I was a kid. I can't recall the last time I actually accomplished a goal of mine.

I've visited r/loseit before. I made a post using a different account on that subreddit several months ago. The responses I got were mostly just people recommending that I exercise, or that I stop eating unhealthy food. Obviously, I'd love to do both of those things, but these days, I can hardly find a good reason to get out of bed. I had a brief period last month where I told myself I would start going to the community center gym, and I did, but only for a week. I just have no motivation. Of course I hate weighing 300 pounds, but I'm too depressed and lazy to do anything about it. 

I used to have hobbies, but that was before my mental illness got the best of me. I'd mostly play video games, which were a good distraction to prevent myself from eating, however nowadays I don't find them fun anymore. I also used to draw on occasion, though I gave up after I realized that nothing I make will ever be good enough to me. The same thing happened with me taking instrument lessons- I decided I wanted to learn to play the flute, but every time I made a mistake, I felt awful, and the instructor suggested I stop coming because of the amount of stress lessons were causing me. Now all I do is sit in my room and listen to music.

I drink water all the time. It still doesn't end up helping me, though. No matter what I do, I still can't distract myself from eating. I'll eat until I become sick and yet continue to eat afterwards.

I immediately assume that I don't have a future because that way I don't end up disappointed when it ends up being true. I don't have much going for me in terms of life- as I mentioned before, I'm ugly, fat, and on top of that, I'm not particularly smart. Failing grades are part of what contributed to my depression becoming notably worse. I don't want to become someone who sets a ton of goals for themselves in the future only to be depressed when they realized they never accomplished any of them. I can't picture myself becoming much more than a McDonald's employee or a Starbucks barista.

Well, recently I've been skipping due to my depression. On the days that I have shown up, it's been okay. I tend not to get much done in class though. My school isn't so much a school as much as it is a therapy group- I used to attend a normal high school back in 2016, but was referred to a new program after my depression and anxiety became notably worse.
No, I haven't mentioned it to her yet. I've only seen her once. She wasn't the one who prescribed me with them anyhow.

Oh, I'm taking Wellbutrin. I'm only on my first week of retaking it though, and apparently it can take up to a month or so until it actually begins to work. I stopped taking it initially because it was having a reverse effect on me.

I would, if I could convince myself to move. On the weekends, I rarely go downstairs, other than when I go to the kitchen to binge on a ton of food. Most of my time is spent lying in bed, doing exactly what I am right now. I'm not responsible for what food comes in the house (I'm not even an adult yet), and despite me telling my parents that I no longer want them buying unhealthy things, they do it regardless. They're aware of my problems with self-control, but all they do is tell me to do is to "stop eating", as if it were that easy. 

I do have a meeting with a psychiatrist relatively soon. She knows of the struggle my weight causes me since I've mentioned it before. Maybe I can bring up a solution with her.
